blogs.title: Cervical Oedema That Is Not an Infection
blogs.description:
Fibrotic muscle inflammation can mimic Ludwig’s angina or idiopathic angio­Edema.
This post outlines how emergency doctors should recognise subtle nailfold erythema,
non‑tender cervical swelling coupled with proximal weakness—and why a rapid glucocorticoid trial becomes warranted even before microbiology proves negative.

blogs.title: Creatine Kinase Is Your Early Red Flag
blogs.description:
A dramatic rise (>10 000 U/L) immediately raises suspicion for inflammatory myopathy.
Even during mild systemic inflammation unaccompanied fever supports pursuing muscle enzymes.
Early CK measurement shifts empathy away from infections towards autoimmune neuromuscular disorders.

blogs.title: Anti‑SAE 1 Antibodies Matter Beyond Glowing Skin Spots
blogs.description:
Anti‑small ubiquitin–like modifier activating enzyme subunit 1 signifies a distinct dermatomyositis phenotype
with higher rates of dysphagia (≈46 %) and interstitial lung disease (≈43 %).
The bad news is its roughly 18 % malignancy association.
Knowing this profile guides both surveillance intensity and therapeutic choices.

blogs.title: Blending Pulse Steroids With Biologics For Severe Dermato​myositis
blogs.description:
High‑dose intravenous methylprednisolone followed by daily prednisone taper,
monthly IVIG infusions,
and B‑cell depletion via rituximab represent current practice
for patients demonstrating airway‐critical dysphagia or profound oedematous manifestation.
The panel discusses dose timing, steroid sparing agents—including choosing mycophenolate over methotrexate
because pulmonary fibrosis is already evident—and PCP prophylaxis modification after hemolytic anaemia develops.

blogs.title: Cancer Screening Checklist When Facing Myopathy Impact
blogs.description:
Using IMACS criteria classify pa­tient into high carcinogenic risk based on disease type,
dysphagia presence,
and specific autoantibodies.
Guidelines recommend chest CT/PET whenever organotropism exists;
in addition upper/lower GI endoscopy every patient should undergo
to rule out occult colorectal neoplasia.
Follow‑up strategy evolves over months depending on tumour marker trends.”}]}
